title: A no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new No Charge work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, category Goodwill, in Estimate.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click "Change Customer" on the customer card.
  3. Pick customer B.
  4. Confirm the change.
  5. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Change Customer window opens.

Step 3:

  • Customer B is picked.

Step 4:

  • The badge reads "Internal" instead of "No Charge".

Step 5:

  • The menu offers no "Change category" and no "Convert to Billable": the category is gone.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R7: “Changing the customer on a work order works as today (not offered on an invoiced or paid billable work order, as today, nor on a closed internal or no-charge work order, S2-R9); until then the classification follows the new customer: to an internal customer the work order becomes internal (prices removed, costs and hours kept, no Convert actions); to a regular customer from an internal one it becomes billable (lines priced as in S2-R6). A No Charge mark and its category survive a change to another regular customer; a no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal and loses its category. The Change Customer dialog says what will happen to the prices and, when the work order stays internal or no charge, adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer]'s minimum ($[amount])." (without 'See Financial Data' the sentence omits the amount).”
